patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports difficulty in combing hair and reaching objects on high shelves for the past few months. Admits to a sedentary lifestyle.

Secondary_Symptoms: Decreased range of motion in shoulder

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diabetes mellitus type II, obesity, hypertension. On metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Sedentary lifestyle, predominately staying indoors and watching television.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies recent injuries or trauma to the arm or shoulder. No fever, weight loss, or other joint involvement.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with stiffness in his arm impacting daily activities.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Doctor, over the past few months I’ve felt stiffness in my arm, and it’s gotten harder to comb my hair and reach things on high shelves. My shoulder range of motion is reduced, and my arm strength feels about 4 out of 5, but I haven’t had any injury or fever.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t noticed any obvious swelling in my joints, just increasing stiffness and trouble moving my shoulder and arm. I’ve mainly been feeling it when I try to comb my hair or reach up high.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, Doctor, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp—just the increasing stiffness when I try to comb my hair.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, Doctor—I haven’t had any itching or a persistent urge to scratch. It’s mainly the stiffness and reduced movement in my shoulder and arm, especially when I try to comb my hair or reach high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble raising your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, yes—raising my arms above my head is difficult, and it’s especially hard on the shoulder when I try to reach or comb my hair.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, Doctor— I haven’t noticed any loss of vision, painful or otherwise. It’s mainly the stiffness in my arm and the reduced shoulder movement when I try to reach overhead, like combing my hair.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had any fever or felt extremely hot, dizzy, or very uncomfortable. It’s been more gradual stiffness in my arm and reduced shoulder movement over the past few months.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed—mostly it’s been gradual stiffness that makes daily tasks harder. I’ve been pretty sedentary and staying indoors, and it’s getting worse over the past few months.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. My main issue is the gradual stiffness in my arm and reduced ability to lift my shoulder—especially when combing my hair or reaching high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had chills or any fever-like symptoms. It’s just been a gradual increase in arm stiffness and reduced shoulder motion over the past few months.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump in your breast that feels firm and hasn’t moved?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t noticed any lump in my breast—no firm, unmoving spot or anything unusual there. My main concern is the gradual stiffness in my arm and reduced shoulder range of motion, especially when I try to comb my hair or reach high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Are you feeling any pain or discomfort on the sides of your abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I don’t have any pain or discomfort on the sides of my abdomen between my ribs and hips. My main problem is the gradual stiffness in my arm and reduced shoulder range of motion, especially when I try to comb my hair or reach high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does that pain go away when you stop walking?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I don’t have pain in my calf when I walk, and it doesn’t go away because I’m not feeling that discomfort. My main issue is the gradual stiffness in my arm with reduced shoulder range of motion, especially when I try to comb my hair or reach up high.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—my urine hasn’t looked darker than usual, and I haven’t noticed any other urinary changes. My main problem is still the gradual stiffness in my arm and trouble lifting my shoulder to comb my hair or reach high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it hard to lift your arm above your head or reach across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, yes—I find it hard to lift my arm above my head and reach across my body, especially when I try to comb my hair or reach items on high shelves. My shoulder feels stiff and my range of motion is clearly reduced, and my arm strength feels weaker than before.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you notice joint pain or stiffness after repeated use, such as after long periods of typing or playing sports?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, yes—after repeated use like trying to comb my hair or reaching up for a while, the stiffness in my arm and reduced shoulder motion feel worse, and my strength seems to drop more than before.”
